title: Closing a project: the project closure workshop
blurb: Explain the closing a project activities in an agile setting and the topics of the project closure workshop, from final demo to handover and benefits.
question: At the end of the final stage, the group demonstrates the finished product, shares lessons, updates documentation and plans handover. Which workshop is this, and what does each topic achieve?

teach.h: A clear end, not a slow drift
teach.body: Closing a project provides a fixed point at which acceptance of the project product is confirmed and the objectives are recognized as achieved (or, if the project ends early, that it closes in an orderly way). It is the last part of the final stage, not a stage of its own. The project manager prepares closure; the board authorizes it in directing a project. The board can also instruct a premature closure when it authorizes a stage or exception plan.
teach.cite: PRINCE2 7 manual 19.1; PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 13.8, Table 13.4

head: Activity
What happens
rows: Who needs to know; final actuals into project log and release map; draft closure notice
Follow-on actions; benefits reviews planned; handover route confirmed
Compare with original and current PID; end project report; lessons report
Brief the board; confirm readiness; note concessions
teach.caption: Paraphrased from Table 13.18. A premature close is prepared differently (PRINCE2 7).

teach.body: In 'confirm project acceptance', the PM and team prepare follow-on action recommendations for unfinished work, issues and risks, check that the benefits management approach includes post-project activities to confirm benefits, and confirm from the PID how products pass to operations. Benefits can be realized during the project through iterative releases, but most are confirmed after closure, so reviews are planned now and carried out later.

items.label: Board ensures reviews cover the product in use

teach.body: Its purpose is to conclude the project formally: confirm the final product meets requirements, reflect on lessons, finalize the documentation and prepare a smooth transition to operations. It also celebrates success and sets guidelines for realizing benefits and for continual improvement.

steps.label: Lessons report
steps.sub: actionable lessons; Agilometer and safety trends

rows.label: Looks at
values: The whole project, at its end

teach.body: Harrowgate Museums Trust's ticketing app is in its final stage. Project manager Marcus Webb updates the project log and release map with final actuals and runs the closure workshop. Visitors' feedback in the final product demo confirms acceptance, teams share lessons, the PID and dashboard are brought up to date, and a handover plan names the venue IT desk as support owner. Executive Joan Ellis's board approves the end project report and confirms that post-project benefits reviews are planned.

teach.text: Closing is NOT a separate stage, and post-project benefits reviews are PLANNED in closing but carried out after the project. Within the closure workshop, the 'progress review' topic finalizes documentation; it is not the progress review workshop used in controlling a stage.

items: Closing: fixed point confirming acceptance of the project product; inside the final stage.
Activities: prepare planned closure, confirm acceptance, evaluate the project, request closure.
Evaluate: compare with original and current PID; end project report; lessons report.
Closure workshop: final product demo, project lessons, progress review, lessons report, final handover planning.
Board authorizes closure: approves end project report, confirms updated canvas.
Most benefits are confirmed after closure.

summary: You can now describe the closing a project activities in agile terms and the purpose and topics of the project closure workshop. You also know where acceptance, lessons, handover and benefits follow-up fit.

A.q: Which topic of the project closure workshop demonstrates the final product for user acceptance?
A.why: The final product demo gathers final feedback and confirms the product meets requirements and is ready for handover (Table 13.19).

whyNot.0: Project lessons shares insights from the project phases.
whyNot.1: The progress review topic updates the project documentation.
whyNot.3: Final handover planning sets support responsibilities and operational requirements.

A.q: In which closing activity does the PM prepare follow-on action recommendations and check that post-project benefit confirmation is planned?
A.why: Confirm project acceptance covers follow-on actions, the benefits management approach and the route to operations (Table 13.18).

whyNot.0: Preparing planned closure updates logs and the release map and drafts the closure notice.
whyNot.2: Evaluating compares the project with the PID and prepares the reports.
whyNot.3: Requesting closure briefs the board and confirms readiness.

A.q: Which closure workshop topic produces a handover plan covering support responsibilities, operational requirements and benefits actions?
A.why: Final handover planning defines clear guidelines for a smooth transition to operations (Table 13.19).

whyNot.0: The demo confirms the product is ready for handover.
whyNot.1: Project lessons shares insights and learnings.
whyNot.2: The lessons report sets actionable lessons for future projects.

B.q: What is the purpose of the 'closing a project' process?
options: A fixed point to confirm acceptance of the project product
A review of the stage before the next one is authorized
A check that the project is viable and worthwhile
A controlled link between the PM and the delivery team
B.why: Closing provides a fixed point at which acceptance of the project product is confirmed (PRINCE2 7 manual 19.1).

whyNot.1: That describes managing a stage boundary.
whyNot.2: That describes starting up a project.

B.q: Which closing activity compares the project with the original PID and approved changes and prepares the end project report and lessons report?
B.why: Evaluate the project reviews the original and current PID, prepares the end project report and puts lessons in the lessons report (Table 13.18).

whyNot.0: Preparing planned closure updates logs with final actuals.
whyNot.1: Requesting closure briefs the board on performance and readiness.
whyNot.2: Confirming acceptance covers follow-on actions and handover.

B.q: Which closure workshop topic updates the PID, project logs, project dashboard and Agilometer so documentation is complete for transition?
B.why: The progress review topic ensures all documentation is accurate and complete for transition (Table 13.19).

whyNot.2: The lessons report defines actionable lessons for future projects.

C.q: Which closure workshop topic should draw on trends from Agilometer and psychological safety assessments, and what does it produce?
options: Project lessons; shared insights and common practices
Progress review; an updated PID and project dashboard
Lessons report; actionable lessons for future projects
Final handover planning; a handover plan for operations
C.why: The lessons report topic defines actionable lessons, including Agilometer and psychological safety trends where possible (Table 13.19).

whyNot.0: Project lessons shares insights; the trends feed the lessons report.
whyNot.1: The progress review updates documentation, including the Agilometer itself.
whyNot.3: Handover planning covers support and operations.

C.q:
Which two statements about closing a project are correct?
1. Closing a project is part of the final stage.
2. Post-project benefits reviews are carried out within closing a project.
3. When authorizing closure, the board confirms the updated project canvas.
4. The closure workshop plans the detailed tasks of a follow-on project.
C.why: Closing happens inside the final stage, and the board confirms the updated project canvas in authorize project closure (Table 13.4).

whyNot.1: Statement 2 is wrong: the reviews are planned now and held after closure.
whyNot.2: Both are wrong: reviews follow closure, and handover planning is not a task plan for a new project.
whyNot.3: Statement 4 is wrong: the workshop prepares handover, not a follow-on project plan.

C.q: In 'prepare planned closure', which artifacts does the PM update with the final stage's actuals?
options: The team plans and team dashboards
The project log and the release map
The project backlog and the canvas
The risk register and the Agilometer
C.why: The PM updates the project log and release map with final actuals and drafts the closure notification (Table 13.18).

whyNot.0: Team plans and dashboards are kept by delivery teams.
whyNot.2: The board confirms the updated canvas at closure; final actuals go in the log and release map.
whyNot.3: The Agilometer is updated in the closure workshop's progress review topic.

reteach.title: Finishing a kitchen renovation
reteach.question: What does a builder do in the last week of a kitchen renovation?

blocks.body: The builder walks the owners round the finished kitchen so they can accept it, the crew talk about what they would do differently, the warranty papers and plans are brought up to date, and the owners are told who to call if a tap leaks. Whether the new kitchen really saves time cooking is judged months later.

blocks.text: Judging the benefit months later mirrors post-project benefits reviews: planned at closure, done afterwards.

explain.body: After planned closure, acceptance and evaluation, the PM requests closure: a briefing on project performance, confirmation of readiness to close, concessions for any off-specifications, and a request to the board.

test.q: What does the PM do in 'request project closure'?
options: Updates logs and the release map with final actuals
Compares the project with the original PID
Briefs the board and confirms readiness to close
test.why: Requesting closure briefs the board on performance, confirms readiness, highlights concessions and requests closure (Table 13.18).

explain.body: The closure workshop formally concludes the project: final product confirmed, lessons reflected on, documentation finalized and transition to operations prepared.

test.q: What is the purpose of the project closure workshop?
options: To assess status and celebrate progress mid-stage
To reflect on the last iteration and improve teamwork
To conclude the project formally and prepare handover
To plan the next stage and define the team OKRs
test.why: The closure workshop ensures the formal conclusion of the project and prepares a smooth transition to operations (13.8.4).

whyNot.0: That is the progress review workshop.
whyNot.3: That is the release planning workshop.

explain.body: Project lessons presents lessons gathered from the project phases and team members to share insights. The lessons report then turns them into actionable lessons for future projects.

test.q: Which closure workshop topic presents lessons gathered from the project phases and individual team members?
test.why: Project lessons presents gathered lessons to share insights and common learnings (Table 13.19).

whyNot.1: The lessons report turns lessons into actions for future projects.

explain.body: Some benefits arrive during the project through iterative releases, but most are confirmed after closure. Closing makes sure the reviews are planned.

test.q: When are most benefits confirmed in a PRINCE2 Agile project?
options: In the final iteration's product demo
test.why: Confirming benefits mostly takes place after closure, although some are realized earlier through releases (6.3.1).

whyNot.0: The demo confirms product acceptance, not benefits.
whyNot.2: The closure workshop sets benefits actions; it does not confirm most benefits.
whyNot.3: The first stage boundary is far too early for most benefits.
